description: Source-bound proposals and analyses awaiting exact replay. None of these entries is a completed Liberpedia experiment. Supplied transcript hashes identify the source notes but the full transcripts are not redistributed here.

reconciled_sources.title: Liber Primus Word Lengths
reconciled_sources.author: Mae
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The historical 2,902-token comparison and its pinned Project Runeberg corpus have a full census and independent checks. This does not cover every word-boundary hypothesis in the thread.

reconciled_sources.title: Observation on rune frequency
reconciled_sources.author: TheScareworkBoo and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The doublet guide recounts the three 4–2–1 groups and clarifies that the 3, 5, 8 numbers are intervening alphabet entries, not start-to-start distances. No cipher operation follows from those counts.

reconciled_sources.title: possible hint/s
reconciled_sources.author: OH and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The fixed LP2-32 grid arrangement reproduces 563, 569 and 1,136 against the 2016 image dimensions and extracted byte length. Later alignments and candidate plaintexts in the thread are separate proposals.

reconciled_sources.title: LP2-39 red-header word suggestions
reconciled_sources.author: tz18 and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The twenty suggested words, including LAW and BEING, were all checked against the three red runes under a specified affine substitution. Other cipher classes and proposed section themes remain untested by that record.

reconciled_sources.title: Do Four... hundred and sixty-four unreasonable things each day
reconciled_sources.author: hcaltrom and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The fixed 464-word, 16-column length-balance statistic and specified comparison corpora are replayed. The thread also proposes grilles, runic selections and other interpretations; those are not established by the balance test.

reconciled_sources.title: 27×27 three-rune-node totient route discussion
reconciled_sources.author: Moon and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The published route replay pins the author repository, checks the 27×27 map and selected arithmetic, and measures how much ciphertext the proposed reading uses. It does not establish that the chosen path is unique or decrypts LP2.

reconciled_sources.title: LP1 magic-square candidate phrase
reconciled_sources.author: Ryry and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The selected PROVE WORTHIER FIND TRUTHS totals, and the segmentation-dependent MYRMELEONTIDAE=809 assignment, have been enumerated from the fixed five candidates. This does not replay the larger 7 MB word corpus or establish a phrase selection rule.

reconciled_sources.title: Magic-square freedom discussion
reconciled_sources.author: igloo party and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The corrected five-degree-of-freedom claim for half-turn-symmetric 5×5 squares with fixed line sums is reproduced by exact rational rank and positive-integer counterexamples. The thread’s outer-ring, date-path and LP2-15 Möbius suggestions are separate.

reconciled_sources.title: OBSCURA table candidate words
reconciled_sources.author: heck and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: All sixteen fixed candidate words and claimed Gematria Primus sums are checked with every exact rune-label segmentation. The proposed word-by-word substitution and full-manuscript transcription audit are not covered.

reconciled_sources.title: LP2-39 dot mirror and spacing discussion
reconciled_sources.author: |vi and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The first two LP2-39 black dots are reproduced as exact horizontal RGB pixel mirrors within declared 32×33 rectangles; dimensions, thresholds and the distinction between edge and center spacing are documented. The same thread’s CicadaOS and binary-spacing proposals are separate.

reconciled_sources.title: Consecutive doublet index-distance report
reconciled_sources.author: LBen and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: The 86-event LP2-00–55 sequence is independently recounted: the reported lag-one 8.81 and lag-three +4 12.9% become 8.6353 and 10/83 (12.05%) under the archived text. A companion replays 20,000 seeded global and page-conditioned shuffles per null, plus selection controls. Its tails are new calculations, not an exact reproduction of the source's 10,000-permutation p-values or proof of a cipher.

reconciled_sources.title: N-rune distances across LP2-00–02
reconciled_sources.author: Zaveon Carlio and participants
reconciled_sources.covered_scope: All successive N-rune gaps on LP2-00–02 are reported under four declared distance and page-boundary conventions, preserving nonprime gaps as dots. The resulting FROM-like fragment does not form a continuous reading and does not verify the signpost interpretation. Artwork-source suggestions in this same discussion remain separate.

entries.title: Grid bytes as a QR or data-matrix image

source.title: An attempt at finding a data matrix in the base60 of pages 49 - 51
source.author: CurtbroG

entries.reported_idea: Convert the LP2-49–51 base-60 pairs to fixed-width bits and plot them as a black-white matrix; the report also describes earlier LP2-15 and solved-page number layouts, a mistaken base-62 pass, and a corrected bit layout.
entries.coverage: The grid guide reproduces base-60 bytes and a fixed 64 by 32 bit rendering. A bounded barcode experiment scans that whole image and its three original page groups under sixteen planar/polarity transforms each: no QR Code or Data Matrix payload decodes, while both positive controls decode. This is a new declared variant, not a replay of every historical image or the earlier page-15 layout.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the report's omitted final images and plotting script for exact historical comparison. Other widths, uncertain glyphs, alternate bit rules, cropped windows and the separate page-15 number rendering require prespecified tests and their own controls.

entries.title: LP2-40 FOR EVERY, reflected florals and a Möbius running key

source.title: Page 40: For Every and the Potential for a Mobius based Running Key
source.author: Scott

entries.reported_idea: Treat FOR EVERY as a candidate red-header reading, combine a shift of 18 and Atbash, interpret floral details as 13 and 31, skip a chosen rune, then investigate a Möbius-directed running/autokey and trigram structure.
entries.coverage: A new source-bound audit verifies the posted shift-18, Atbash and prime-minus-one arithmetic for FOR EVERY. Those fixed layers match zero of seven non-F archived ciphertext positions; the residual key is calculated from the target. The proposed Möbius state rule and its later variations remain unspecified, so no complete decryption has been replayed.
entries.replay_needed: Snapshot the changing spreadsheet or provide a complete fixed state table; specify the Möbius argument, starting point, sign/zero handling, key clock and skipped-rune rule before computing new ciphertext. Then score an untouched continuation against matched controls.

entries.title: Six F interrupters and periodic IoC on LP2-54–55

source.title: IoC analysis with interrupters for pages 54-55
source.author: Lanfear

entries.reported_idea: Enumerate 64 settings of six F positions under two ciphertext-autokey interruption rules and compare periodic IoC, especially a reported period-13 peak.
entries.coverage: Two published, independently checked records enumerate all 64 masks of the six fixed F positions, periods 2–30, for explicit ciphertext-autokey reset and skip rules. Both find an unmasked period-13 peak that does not exceed their matched search controls. These are new implementations; the source scripts and plots were not supplied.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the reported source code and plots to determine its exact recurrence, period range, IoC denominator and position conventions. Compare those original outputs directly with the published reset and skip traces; do not attribute our controlled p-values to the historical post.

entries.title: Alberti disks, rule transitions and branching on LP2-39

source.title: Leon Alberti’s disk cipher and Liber Primus
source.author: |vi

entries.reported_idea: Apply cover-derived disk correspondences and four rotation rules, a reported 5-6-3-11 sequence, and dot-triggered branches to LP2-39 rows. The transcript refers to separate method and test PDFs not present in the supplied text.
entries.coverage: A bounded source audit reproduces the cited LP2-39 row and signed shift totals. Ordinary modulo 31 yields right-hand residues 29 and 23, while the post gives positive 2 and 8; reversing direction would be an additional rule. The full disk alphabets, transitions and branch selection are still unavailable, so the proposed reading has not been replayed.
entries.replay_needed: Freeze both disk alphabets, each state transition and branch-selection rule before testing a complete row against known-reading and shuffled controls. The arithmetic audit is not a disk decryption.

entries.title: QuagMirrors with Möbius-selected keywords and autokey
entries.reported_idea: Use three thematic words as keyed alphabets, choose mappings with Möbius values related to primes and totients, and compose a modified autokey before the keyed substitution.
entries.coverage: A pinned source-version replay reproduces the draft program's first six LP2-00 outputs, DCBWJO. The source then stops intentionally; it does not supply a complete-page result or held-out continuation.
entries.replay_needed: Specify how the draft continues beyond its six-rune break, freeze every override and compare a complete output with an untouched continuation and matched controls.

entries.title: Cover rotations and a compass-based substitution
entries.reported_idea: Use cover and marginalia orientations as a rotating cipher framework; the thread mentions 180-degree turns as an Atbash operation and additional compass interpretations explained in a linked video.
entries.coverage: The shared-radii experiment measures one fixed geometric construction on two pages, not the linked video's cipher procedure.
entries.replay_needed: Transcribe the video into a finite rune-by-rune algorithm with page scope, rotation order and starting state; reproduce a known reading before testing an unsolved passage and preserve all tested orientations.

entries.title: Word-search routes and missing primes in the 256-cell grid

source.title: A Different Lens on the Liber Primus 256 Table
source.author: Dc0Y

entries.reported_idea: Search the grid in compass-like directions for word-like and number patterns, including reported absences of 3301, 1033 and 2213, and explore four 8 by 8 quadrants and reflected five-dot shapes.
entries.coverage: The four-cell decimal-prime search is reproduced on the original 32 × 8 grid, alternate 16 × 16 and fixed-quadrant layouts, with shuffled-digit controls. Suffix-word routes and five-dot artwork constraints remain untested.
entries.replay_needed: Freeze a suffix-word dictionary and route rule or a specific five-dot geometric constraint before testing those separate parts of the proposal.

entries.title: Large line gaps, punctuation and JPEG size

source.title: An analysis of the Big Gaps found in the Liber Primus
source.author: CurtbroG

entries.reported_idea: Measure unusually large gaps between rune rows, associate them with punctuation or number panels, and compare JPEG sizes. The report gives 109 versus 73 pixels for a typical gap and a different parable-page measurement.
entries.coverage: The wiki has page-region observations and a JPEG-size audit, but no full source-pinned replay of the report's exact gap-coordinate census or its claimed punctuation association.
entries.replay_needed: Pin the exact JPEG versions, define row bounding boxes and gap statistic for every page, verify the reported 109/73 values and exceptional page, then compare the punctuation association without selecting pages after inspection.

entries.title: Proposed mechanisms for scarce adjacent doublets

source.title: List of ways to reduce doublets
source.author: ozon

entries.reported_idea: Compare additive, Beaufort and multiplicative ciphertext feedback with deletion, insertion and reordering as distinct explanations for the low doublet rate.
entries.coverage: The archive now tests uniform additive keys, fixed single-rune deletion, literal additive/Beaufort/subtractive feedback identities, literal multiplicative feedback, and page-anchored block-boundary placement. Multiplication fails at 450 zero-to-nonzero edges; sizes 5, 7 and 13 show no boundary enrichment under fixed-count controls. These are narrower tests, not a replay of every proposed mechanism.
entries.replay_needed: Define and test the remaining inserted filler symbols, dynamic key switching, and zero-skip/reset variants separately. Each needs a complete reversible rule and held-out reading control.

entries.title: 729-cell cross-section inversion and fractional rune choices
entries.reported_idea: Use 729 divided by a rune's ordinal, reduce modulo 29, then choose among base and line-dependent neighboring rune labels from the fractional part. The post allows further letter rearrangement and removal to interpret output.
entries.coverage: A new source-bound audit traces 729 divided by the zero-based GP index at every archived rune position. It confirms the 729-rune total and identifies the worked first word's index-28 use for prime 107, whose canonical zero-based index is 27. It also quantifies 34 undefined F positions and the effect of unspecified line and wrap conventions. It does not reproduce the post's manual letter rearrangement or claimed reading.
entries.replay_needed: Recover or fix one rule for F, line-clock reset, out-of-range indices, neighbor selection and permitted postprocessing. Then compare complete unedited output and a held-out continuation with declared language controls. The 27×27 totient-map route is a separate algorithm.

entries.title: Möbius-of-totient zero mask and proposed LP2-00 reading

source.title: Theory for Solving the First Page of Liber Primus, using Mobius(totient) = 0
source.author: di

entries.reported_idea: Assign each rune prime p the value μ(φ(p)), preserve zero-category positions across a candidate decoding, and use word-list search plus thematic word selection to propose a reading of LP2-00.
entries.coverage: A bounded control now checks the stated one-way zero constraint on the known LP2-56 prime-minus-one reading: 28 of 85 ciphertext-zero runes become plaintext nonzero. The proposed LP2-00 sentence and its dictionary filtering have not been replayed.
entries.replay_needed: Check other known pairs separately, pin the original dictionary/code and rune spelling rules, count all candidate words per LP2-00 position, then test the proposed sentence on untouched rows and matched random masks.

entries.title: JPEG byte histograms and alleged null-heavy page classes

source.title: Hex Value Distribution in the Unsolved Pages
source.author: CurtbroG

entries.reported_idea: Classify JPEG byte-value histograms into null-heavy and more even-looking sets; the report names LP2-00, 04, 24 and 26 as the latter and asks whether encoding mode explains the grouping.
entries.coverage: The archived-file audit counts all 256 byte values for all 58 LP2 and 17 LP1 JPEGs and reproduces the reported four-page LP2 split. A separate fixed-quality re-encode control changes the modal-byte classes, so the original split is not stable under those JPEG encodings. Component count does not explain the original split. The exact 2023 source revision and missing histogram screenshots remain unverified.
entries.replay_needed: Recover or pin the cited repository revision and original screenshots to compare byte-for-byte inputs and subjective “null-star” categories. Any proposed encoded message needs a fixed extraction rule and matched controls; the histogram grouping alone is not one.

entries.title: LP2-54–55 header crib under ciphertext and plaintext autokey
entries.reported_idea: Use the red one-rune plus eight-rune header as a constrained crib, enumerate candidate words with exactly eight GP runes, and test explicit ciphertext-feedback versus plaintext-feedback recurrences. The discussion corrects a confusion between those two clocks; it does not provide a completed candidate census.
entries.coverage: A fixed-rule baseline now enumerates all 29 primers under each of the discussion's explicit ciphertext- and plaintext-feedback recurrences, with complete LP2-54 outputs and the six A/I/O openings. Earlier LP2-54–55 experiments assess F-interruption rules by periodic IoC. None enumerates eight-rune dictionary words, the source's unspecified C/K/D functions or a held-out reading.
entries.replay_needed: Pin a word list and transliteration rule for eight-rune candidates, then define each additional C/K/D function before searching. Count all tried functions and words, run a known-reading control, and test any selected candidate on untouched continuation; report every candidate rather than only readable snippets.

entries.title: 2,883-rune Spirals–Branches stream alignment

source.title: Spirals and Branches equal-length stream discussion
source.author: heck, Joel, and Vatoshi Vergamoto

entries.reported_idea: Align the reported 2,883-rune Spirals-plus-Spiral-Branches stream with an equally long constructed stream; variants include forward pairing, reversal of Branches, an Atbash transform on its second half, and modular subtraction. A posted plain-rune transcription and proposed variants appear in the thread, but no complete scored sweep is preserved there.
entries.coverage: The two rune strings pasted in the supplied discussion match the archived Spirals and Branches-plus-heading streams exactly. A new bounded experiment pairs them with the F-omitted Spiral Branches stream and tests five direct, retrograde and Atbash subtraction variants. Its best IoC is not unusual under exhaustive shifts or page-conditioned shuffles. This does not cover every operator, offset or proposed score in the source thread.
entries.replay_needed: Any broader claim needs a fixed list of additional operations (such as addition, multiplication or XOR), permitted shifts, F treatment and a declared language or n-gram score. Repeat the entire expanded selection under matched controls, and verify any candidate reading on untouched text.

entries.title: LP2-15 word sums, nearest-prime distances and reverse-add palindromes
entries.reported_idea: Map each word's GP sum to its distance from a nearest prime, concatenate those distances under selected zero separators, and add the resulting decimal number to its digit reversal. The thread reports several palindromes and later corrects an earlier 46-digit claim to 53 digits.
entries.coverage: The reported 53-digit reverse-add equality and its fixed-digit shuffle control are reproduced. A companion audit now derives all 57 first-section word distances from the hashed LP2-15–16 transcription and compares every digit with the reported 53. The complete archive-derived sequence also yields a palindrome, but the source report does not specify how its shorter sequence was obtained.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the author's exact transcription or omitted-word rule to explain the 53-versus-57 difference. A cipher claim would then need a fixed use of the distances on unsolved text, with all selected section and grouping choices included in its control.

entries.title: First-release star marks and artwork layering
entries.reported_idea: Examine faint star-shaped marks in the LP1 background and whether later text or illustration layers truncate them; the discussion contrasts deliberate markers with production artifacts and mentions grayscale printing as a visibility aid.
entries.coverage: The visual index hosts original page images but does not map these marks, test the claimed occlusions, or identify a source artwork or software operation.
entries.replay_needed: Identify all affected original JPEGs and mark coordinates at native resolution. Compare unmodified pixels, fixed contrast views and layer-boundary crops; record counterexamples on the same pages. Distinguish observable occlusion from an inferred editing chronology.

entries.title: Night Thoughts as a 729-rune book-code source
entries.reported_idea: Use the 729 runes in LP2-00–02 as a pointer into Edward Young’s Night Thoughts, possibly in an illustrated Blake edition. The discussion points to a line 729 in one Night and explores matching imagery and wording.
entries.coverage: A source audit reproduces the 729-rune count and locates all six quoted passages in a pinned 1853 Gilfillan text. Five are verse line 729 there; the Night IX quotation is line 731. This is an edition-specific comparison, not verification of the different linked Google Books scan or a cipher use.
entries.replay_needed: Pin the Google Books scan or other intended edition, then verify all six line coordinates in that source. Any cipher claim needs a fixed line extraction, text normalization, target span and complete-output control.

entries.title: Totients before the LP2-15 prime-gap construction
entries.reported_idea: Starting from the page-15 square, apply Euler’s totient to a prime-related sequence, subtract values from 3301, and interpret the resulting gaps as a Fibonacci arrangement. The thread then proposes applying corresponding manipulations to rune text.
entries.coverage: A source-bound audit compares all sixteen cells in the posted arrays. The prime candidates fit after two addition choices despite a subtraction label; one specified predecessor gap is 317 in the source but computes to 377. No forward rune rule is supplied.
entries.replay_needed: Freeze sign selection, repeated prime-index handling, panel traversal and a rune operation before testing an untouched target. Retain the source's 317/377 disagreement and uncertain cell.

entries.title: Reverse and table-canon readings of Cicada music

source.title: Music structure, reversal and watermark discussion
source.author: Nostalgico and participants

entries.reported_idea: Reverse a named track, join it to its forward version, and test a table-canon reading; the thread also describes rhythmic alignments between instruments and repetition in The Instar Emergence.
entries.coverage: Music references and general audio methods do not replay this particular transform or establish a decoded message. The source conversation does not fix the exact audio master, alignment, voices or acceptance criterion.
entries.replay_needed: Pin source-file hashes and sample rate; choose the track, reversal boundary, instrument separation and canonical alignment in advance; publish waveform/spectrogram and exact output, including negative controls made from other tracks.

entries.title: Acoustic watermark search in Cicada tracks

source.title: Music structure, reversal and watermark discussion
source.author: Nostalgico and participants

entries.reported_idea: Look for a deliberately embedded acoustic watermark in the published music. The discussion raises this as a question rather than giving a detector, payload or reported extraction.
entries.coverage: No watermark-specific detector result is recorded. Existing file-steganography and audio-method guides cover other mechanisms and cannot be used as evidence for this proposal.
entries.replay_needed: Choose specific original files and hashes, state the watermark family and detector parameters, record a detection threshold before inspection, and compare positives and false positives on matched non-Cicada audio.

entries.title: Dictionary-wide word fitting to LP1 magic-square totals
entries.reported_idea: Enumerate English words by rune length and Gematria Primus total, fit them to selected LP1 square cells, then look for a coherent phrase or clue. The thread links a separate word corpus and reports selected readings.
entries.coverage: The fixed phrase and MYRMELEONTIDAE arithmetic are checked. A separate control now counts every GP-131 and GP-151 candidate in a preserved 138,466-row revision of 1_grams-full and shows 216,600 ordered four-slot combinations after fixing the proposed rune lengths. The source transcript’s older data/1_grams link is stale; the surviving corpus is not proven identical to its reported worddata.csv, and no historical phrase-selection search was replayed.
entries.replay_needed: Recover or identify the reported worddata.csv; fix vocabulary, rune segmentation, cell positions, word order and a semantic scoring rule before selection; retain every phrase and compare scores against equally flexible square and word-list controls. A separate LP2 key test needs a fixed cipher transform and held-out target.

entries.title: Use OBSCURA-table GP matches as word-specific keys
entries.reported_idea: For an encrypted word with the same Gematria Primus sum as a value in the LP1-05 table, use a candidate table word to decrypt that word only. A participant reports trying matching words and several operations without a saved positive result.
entries.coverage: The fixed sixteen OBSCURA-table word sums are checked, but matching an additive total is many-to-one. The thread does not define the transform, word boundaries or all operations tried; no current record tests this word-specific mapping.
entries.replay_needed: Fix one LP2 target and transcription, one rune-sum matching policy, the permitted table-word candidates and exact transform; log every output, including failures, then compare with matched random word keys of equal length and value.

entries.title: Manual rune-by-rune transcription recheck
entries.reported_idea: Compare manuscript images against stored transcriptions rune by rune. One participant says they checked LP2-00–02; others propose a full manual audit and mention solved-page errors, but the supplied thread contains no coordinate-level correction register.
entries.coverage: The site documents specific stored corrections and quantifies their impact on word lengths and IoC. That is narrower than a complete image-to-text audit of every manuscript page and does not verify the reported private checks.
entries.replay_needed: For each original image, publish page, row, character coordinate, transcribed symbol, disputed alternative and adjudication with cropped evidence; have a second reader independently check disputed marks and page-spanning word boundaries.

entries.title: Cuneiform numbers as pointers to CicadaOS 560 files
entries.reported_idea: Use the cuneiform sexagesimal readings 1033 = 17×60+13 and 3301 = 55×60+1 to motivate trying CicadaOS files named _560.00, _560.13 and _560.17 against the cuneiform pages, potentially by XOR or another previously used file operation.
entries.coverage: The cuneiform guide checks the printed numbers, but no fixed file-to-page mapping or byte transform follows from the numeric resemblance. The thread poses the application as a question; it does not report a complete test.
entries.replay_needed: Pin ISO and file hashes, specify which numbered file pairs with which page and how images become byte streams, fix offsets, XOR/key advancement and output acceptance before testing, then run all declared pairings and comparison file numbers.

entries.title: Thick and thin LP2 spaces as a binary channel
entries.reported_idea: Classify visibly thick and thin word or line gaps as two symbols, then read them as bits. The discussion also offers a mundane typography mechanism: apostrophes, quotation marks and other fallback-font glyphs may change line metrics.
entries.coverage: A bounded audit measures the LP2-15 number-panel line gaps on the original JPEG and compares selected nearby text-line gaps. Its wider final panel gap survives threshold changes. The source screenshots are unavailable, so the proposed word-gap bitstream and fallback-font explanation remain untested.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the original word-gap screenshots or fix page and glyph coordinates before testing a binary classification, byte order and font/layout controls.

entries.title: Möbius transform of LP2-15 panel numbers
entries.reported_idea: Apply the Möbius function to the numbers at the top of LP2-15 and inspect the resulting arrangement. The supplied thread refers to an image of the output without retaining its pixels or a full interpretation rule.
entries.coverage: A new panel audit applies arithmetic Möbius μ(n) to all sixteen printed cells in original row order, with a factorization ledger and independent checker. Twelve outputs are zero and the four nonzero values occupy row two. The source's referred-to image is absent, so its exact historical output cannot be compared; no subsequent cipher operation was specified.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the original output image for exact historical comparison. Before treating this as a key, specify a traversal, zero handling, a rule mapping μ values to rune operations, and a complete-text control without adapting those choices to output.

entries.title: Rune indices or word sums packed as bytes
entries.reported_idea: Encode rune indices, prime values or per-word GP sums as integers, pack them into bytes and inspect the output as a file or possible program. The pasted discussion proposes variants but does not report that any resulting file was produced or executed.
entries.coverage: The grid direct-byte test concerns printed LP2-49–51 base-60 values, not a whole rune stream or word sums. No pinned packing width, bit order or artifact from this suggestion is in the archive.
entries.replay_needed: Fix the exact page range and whether inputs are indices, primes or word sums; declare word boundaries, integer width, byte order, padding and expected file signatures before generating all variants. Treat file recognition as a bounded data test, not evidence that arbitrary bytes should be executed.

entries.title: Five-dot pattern overlaid on a rune paragraph
entries.reported_idea: Place a five-dot drawing over a manuscript paragraph, perhaps after rotation, and read selected rune positions. A participant reports that an overlay seemed close in size but did not quite work; the thread later compares the marks with constellations and a historical symbolic alphabet.
entries.coverage: The dot guide records the locations and relationships of the manuscript marks, but the pasted source substitutes 'Image' placeholders for the particular overlay and does not give selected rune coordinates or an output string.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the original overlay and identify both source page and target paragraph. Pin image scale, rotation, registration points and rune-selection tolerance; publish selected positions and compare with other rotations and matched five-point patterns.

entries.title: Partial website sweep against LP2-56's hash
entries.reported_idea: Check pages of metafysica.nl against the 128-hex-character LP2-56 hash. One participant says they visited about half the pages with a hash-alarm browser add-on active; no URL list, bytes, hash convention or complete result table is supplied.
entries.coverage: A partial visit report cannot establish which pages were tested or exclude the site. Liberpedia's other hash experiments test their own pinned corpora, not this website snapshot.
entries.replay_needed: Pin a date-stamped URL manifest and exact response bytes; specify SHA-512 versus any alternate algorithm and whether to hash raw responses, rendered text or normalized content. Save every URL, byte hash and comparison, including redirects and inaccessible pages.

entries.title: Selecting words after thousands of cipher combinations
entries.reported_idea: A participant reports applying roughly 5,000 cipher combinations to unsolved 5.jpg and choosing English words at many word slots, allowing the combination to vary between words. The pasted output is a discontinuous selected-word string; the thread itself questions whether the selected words form a coherent message.
entries.coverage: The archive has general search-maximum and crib controls, but not the reported list of 5,000 combinations, their raw outputs or the choices that assembled this string. It is a reported search, not a reproduced reading.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the complete combination list, exact page transcription and tokenizer, every candidate output, the per-slot selection rule and any manual edits. Replay the same selection pipeline on fixed controls, score whole sentences and held-out text, and count how often short common words appear without a correct decryption.

entries.title: Solved-text wording as proposed section-title cribs

source.title: Its words are the map, their meaning is the road
source.author: heck and participants

entries.reported_idea: Use repeated wording in solved passages (WITHIN, DIVINITY, ALL THINGS and INTUS) to nominate unsolved section headings or red-header cribs. The thread also suggests DEEP WITHIN for the four-plus-five LP2-15 heading and A PROCEDURE for the LP2-33 Cuneiform opening. A separate suggestion matches the GP sum of DJU BEI AE to OF ALL THNGS at 389.
entries.coverage: The stored GP alphabet gives 389 for D+J+U+B+E+I+AE and for O+F+A+L+L+TH+NG+S; ordinary THINGS adds an I. DEEP WITHIN is length-compatible with the LP2-15 heading under literal GP encoding, but length alone is not decryption. The literal LP2-33 opening is two plus eight runes, whereas A PROCEDURE encodes as one plus nine under the ordinary GP spelling, so that proposed placement needs an additional boundary or spelling rule. No one transformation or untouched continuation has been supplied for these guesses.
entries.replay_needed: Identify the exact manuscript heading/runes for each proposed crib; pin GP segmentation, the THNGS spelling, and any boundary change needed for A PROCEDURE. Select the crib list and transformation before examining output. Count equal-sum alternatives and require one rule to predict untouched text or another page.

entries.title: 464-word indexing and a proposed STUDY HERE pointer

source.title: Koan and Gematria Primus arithmetic discussion
source.author: Fib, heck and participants

entries.reported_idea: Number a reported 464-word solved list in both directions and read positions 133 and 331 as STUDY HERE; divide a corresponding encrypted-word list into 133 and 331 words, whose GP sums are reported as primes 26,893 and 71,963. The thread connects 464 with the ordinal of 3301 and a 928-word carrier.
entries.coverage: A bounded pointer record finds STUDY HERE at five positions in the archived 464-word reading. The selected 331/133 cut gives 72,065 and 26,893, so only the second reported sum reproduces; the first differs by 102. The reporter’s exact word list is unavailable.
entries.replay_needed: Recover the reporter’s original 464-word ciphertext list and transcription to locate the 102-point difference in the first block. Keep the 331/133 index choice and the already-solved STUDY HERE phrase separate from any proposed new pointer, and quantify plausible phrase matches across other split choices.

entries.title: Transform earlier poster coordinates to search for the signpost
